summary:
Trends is the category to trust right now across every rating — 9-3 (75%, n=12) over the last 14 days with a 5-game win streak on all four models, and it's the best long-term combo piece too (trends+sp hits 57.9% at n=636, trends+runs 57.2% at n=701). Hitting is the other hot hand, running 67-58% across R1-R3 over the same window, while SP and bullpen are both ice cold at 42% (5-7) across the board — if a play leans heavily on starting pitcher or bullpen ratings without trends backing it, discount it today. R2 is the sharpest model to lean on right now: it's 5-2 (71%, +2.0u) in strong plays over 14 days and 9-3 (75%, +8.0u) over 30, best combination of recent heat and volume among the four.

Today's slate is a single game, but it's a clean one for the model: TBR @ MIL, and all four ratings converge on MIL, with conviction building from R1 (+0.25) up through R4 (+0.89) for full consensus. That ascending delta pattern — where the higher-numbered models show more confidence — has tracked with the 30-day strong-play trend, where R3 and R4 have posted 75% and 56% respectively on fewer but more selective plays. MIL is also the single best team-when-liked in the data: 48-22 (69%, n=70) overall and 27-12 (69%, +18.0u) specifically on strong plays, making this about as favorable a team/rating intersection as the model offers. With trends and hitting both running hot and MIL carrying the top team-volume record in the sample, this is a spot where the signal stack lines up instead of fighting itself — bullpen and SP are cold, but the consensus here isn't being driven by those categories. Treat this as a trust-the-board day: one game, full agreement, and the hottest category plus the best-performing team both pointing the same direction.
